question: As per the India Justice Report, 2025, which is the only state in India to meet all three (SC, ST and OBC) quotas in both the police and judiciary?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India Justice Report (IJR) 2025** identifies **Karnataka** as the standout performer in maintaining social diversity within its justice delivery system.
 
• It is currently the **only state in India** to have successfully met the prescribed reservation quotas for **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **Other Backward Classes (OBC)** in both its **Police** department and the **Judiciary**.
 
• In the **Police** pillar, **Karnataka** has demonstrated a consistent ability to fill **reserved vacancies**, ensuring that the law enforcement agency reflects the demographic composition of the state.
 
• In the **Judiciary** pillar, particularly at the **subordinate court level**, the state has adhered to the **Constitutional mandates** of representation for marginalized communities, which is a rare feat across Indian states.
 
• Overall, **Karnataka** ranked **first** among the 18 large and mid-sized states in the **India Justice Report**, maintaining its leadership position in the overall capacity to deliver justice. ***Hence, the correct answer is Karnataka.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About India Justice Report (IJR):**
 
 
• The **IJR** is a first-of-its-kind initiative launched in **2019** by **Tata Trusts** in collaboration with partners such as **Centre for Social Justice**, **Common Cause**, **Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative**, **DAKSH**, **TISS-Prayas**, and **Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy**.
 
• It tracks the **capacity** of states to deliver justice based on **four pillars**: **Police**, **Prisons**, **Judiciary**, and **Legal Aid**.
 
• The report uses **government data** to assess states on various parameters including **budgets**, **human resources**, **workload**, **diversity**, **infrastructure**, and **trends** over the last five years.
 
 
 
• **Diversity and Representation:**
 
 
• The report highlights that **diversity** is a crucial indicator of a fair justice system. Nationally, most states struggle to meet **SC, ST, and OBC** quotas, leading to significant **vacancies**.
 
• While **Karnataka** leads in caste-based quotas, the report also examines **Women in Justice**. It notes that while the share of women is increasing, they still represent a small fraction of the **Police** and **Judiciary** at higher levels across **India**.
 
 
 
• **Performance of Other States:**
 
 
• In the **2025** ranking, states like **Tamil Nadu**, **Telangana**, and **Gujarat** followed **Karnataka** in the top tier of large states.
 
• Smaller states like **Sikkim** and **Arunachal Pradesh** are ranked separately, with **Sikkim** often performing well in the small states category.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• The reservation for **SC, ST, and OBC** in public employment and services is backed by **Articles 15(4)** and **16(4)** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• Ensuring representation in the **Judiciary** and **Police** is vital for maintaining the **Rule of Law** and building **public trust** in the state's institutions.
 
 
 
• **Key National Findings:**
 
 
• Despite the progress in **Karnataka**, the **IJR 2025** points out a **national trend** of rising **pendency** of cases and chronic **under-staffing** in prisons and courts.
 
• The average vacancy in **High Courts** remains high at nearly **30%**, and the **Police-to-Population ratio** remains below international standards in many states.
 
• The report serves as a **policy tool** for **State Governments** and the **Union Government** to address systemic gaps in the **Indian justice system**.
